goal: Reviewer can distinguish retry, retest, and regression and close a failure only after required regression passes.

acceptance_ownership.AC-06: Task 020 owns the append-only lifecycle history that distinguishes first failure, retry, repair, retest, and regression without overwriting prior attempts or evidence.
acceptance_ownership.AC-07: Task 020 owns deterministic FLAKY and PASS AFTER FIX labels derived from attempt kind, immutable fingerprints, completed repair facts, and fresh evidence.
acceptance_ownership.AC-15: Task 004 owns retry fingerprint validation. Task 020 must invoke and regression-test that validator before accepting a retry.
acceptance_ownership.AC-26: Task 022 owns the concrete repaired, impacted, and baseline rerun scope. Task 020 must consume the exact required case set before proposing closure.
acceptance_ownership.AC-27: Task 020 owns deterministic routing to a Core break-loop proposal from a trusted Task 018 no-progress signal. Core alone owns the governance decision and lifecycle transition.

non_goals: Do not expand beyond this vertical slice or complete dependent tasks implicitly.
Do not add fallback, verification light mode, manual green overrides, or business-project package mutations.
Do not overwrite failed attempts, raw evidence, or unrelated downstream worktree changes.
expected_evidence: A focused failing test or fixture before the implementation change
System-executed command output with exit status
Task report, spec review, and quality review before checkbox completion
Direct evidence for AC-06, AC-07, and AC-27 plus regression evidence that Task 004 AC-15 and Task 022 AC-26 contracts are consumed without duplication
unsafe_assumptions: Tool availability is not runtime readiness.
Model interpretation is not a deterministic oracle.
Report HTML is not the release gate source.
Legacy V1 status is not V2 proof.
stop_condition: Stop when dependencies 018-failure-classification, 019-development-repair-bridge, 022-case-rerun-impact are incomplete, scope or contract evidence is missing, a required dependency is unavailable, or shared kernel behavior would be duplicated.
